I know it’s dirty—that’s why I’m there to clean it—but my mind keeps circling back: *What if I carry something home on my clothes? What if I touch my face without realizing?* I scrub my hands at work more than I need to, and I changed my uniform routine—now I leave my work shoes outside the back door, and I shower the second I get home, even if I’m exhausted. It doesn’t feel optional. 

I don’t know if it’s grief or just this job, but I’ve been turning thoughts over and over—about him, about the trains, about sickness. Some nights, I lie there thinking the same thing for hours: *Did I touch that rail? Could I have inhaled something?* It’s not like I feel sad all the time, but I don’t feel like myself either. I just keep going over things, doing the same things in the same way, just in case. It’s not exactly fear, and it’s not exactly despair—just this constant loop I can’t step out of.
